record.original_question: In the rank-one case, let J be a division Jordan algebra and let St(J) be the associated rank-one Steinberg group considered for the Jordan pair (J, J). Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J except when J is the finite field F_q with q in {2, 3, 4, 9}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A Jordan algebra J over a commutative ring of scalars is called a division Jordan algebra if every nonzero element of J is invertible (equivalently, every nonzero x ∈ J has a U-operator U_x that is bijective). To any Jordan algebra J one associates the Jordan pair V = (J, J) with quadratic operators given by the U-operators of J; if J is a division Jordan algebra then V is a division Jordan pair. To such a rank-one Jordan pair (J, J) one associates the Steinberg group St(J), defined by generators and relations encoding the rank-one commutator/inversion relations of the projective elementary group of (J, J). The group St(J) maps onto the projective elementary group of (J, J), and one says St(J) is centrally closed if this central extension is universal, i.e., St(J) is its own universal central extension (equivalently, it is perfect with trivial Schur multiplier in the appropriate category).

Question. Determine whether St(J) is centrally closed for every division Jordan algebra J, with the only exceptions being the cases in which J is the finite field F_q for q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 9} (regarded as a Jordan algebra under its commutative associative product). In particular, prove or disprove that St(J) is centrally closed whenever J is a division Jordan algebra not isomorphic to F_q for q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 9}.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the introductory survey on Steinberg groups for Jordan pairs (Loos–Neher program). Available sources—including Loos's "Rank one groups and division pairs" and the Loos–Neher monograph—develop the framework of central closedness for root-graded cases but do not record a resolution of the rank-one division-Jordan-algebra question outside the listed small finite-field exceptions. No subsequent paper found in the search announces a proof or counterexample.
